subject.title: [Bug]:  Isolated cron session agent loop continues consuming tokens after run marked "ok"

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-after-run by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only contract with explicit recovery for existing jobs?
rationale: Current main leaves the reported leak possible, but the two open PRs choose incompatible lifecycle semantics and both affect existing cron configuration behavior.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Proceed with the linked fix direction, but require it to cover already-persisted omitted values or provide an explicit doctor/operator recovery path.

options.title: Keep one-shot-only deleteAfterRun
options.body: Pause or close the linked defaulting PR and continue through a strict-validation path that aligns CLI, Gateway, UI, docs, and legacy recovery.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only cleanup
options.body: Land only the new-job default and document that existing omitted jobs need manual edit or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked fix direction, but require it to cover already-persisted omitted values or provide an explicit doctor/operator recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the adjacent cleanup path and is the best available routing candidate from the inspected history for the cron lifecycle contract decision.
